_meta.rule: Charter-school positions are not scored on the education axis ("Should public school money follow students to private schools?"); also vague "educational choices" with no mention of public money for private schools. Kept: statements that explicitly cover vouchers, ESAs, or school choice beyond charters (e.g. steve-hilton).
_meta.editorNote: editorNote is internal only; merge_gapfill.py does not copy it.

unsure.summary: He backs local control of schools, including charter schools. Charter schools are public schools, so this doesn't say whether public money should go to private schools.
unsure.quote: I support local control of schools including charter schools and any other system that protects parents’ rights to ensure their child gets a great education. We are punishing low-income children by forcing them to stay in underperforming schools.
unsure.sourceTitle: Campaign website (bofrench.com, 2016 Texas House race; quoted by Ballotpedia)
unsure.editorNote: Replaces education +3. The quote names charter schools and "any other system that protects parents' rights" but never vouchers, ESAs, school choice with public money, or private schools. Same standard as Bush and Becker. Source is Ballotpedia (403 from this box), so the quote was not re-read this pass.

unsure.summary: She opposes federal money for privately run charter schools. Charter schools are public schools, so this doesn't say whether public money should go to private schools.
unsure.quote: I oppose new federal funding to privately run charter schools and oppose steps to facilitate the expansion of charter schools.
unsure.editorNote: Replaces education -4. "Privately run" refers to charter operators; charters are publicly funded public schools, so this is not a position on public money for private schools.

unsure.summary: She backs more charter schools and "more educational choices" but doesn't say whether public money should go to private schools.
unsure.quote: I support expanding charter schools, modernizing curriculum, reducing administrative overhead, and giving parents more educational choices.
unsure.editorNote: Replaces education +4. Only explicit content is charter expansion; "more educational choices" is too vague to read as vouchers/ESAs (contrast Steve Hilton, kept: "introducing school choice" beyond charters).

unsure.quote: Charter schools can play a limited role, but they should not undermine public school funding, equity, or stability.
unsure.editorNote: Replaces education -3. Questionnaire question asks only about charter schools; page has no voucher/private-school text (checked 2026-10-30).
